seoTitle: Squarespace Text Highlight Effects and Animation Guide
metaDescription: Highlight, underline, or animate text in Squarespace to draw attention to headlines and important messages on your site.
intro: Beyond basic fade or slide animations, Squarespace also lets you apply highlight and underline effects to specific text to draw a reader's eye to important content. This guide covers opening the text editor, selecting a portion of text, and applying an effect.

steps.heading: Log in and open your site
steps.body: Sign in to Squarespace, select the website you want to edit, and enter the editor by locating the Edit button.

steps.heading: Find the text block to edit
steps.body: Navigate to the page containing the text, hover over it, and click the edit icon that appears.

steps.heading: Highlight the specific text
steps.body: Select the portion of text you want to style, the same way you would in a word processor, before applying any effect.

steps.heading: Apply a highlight or animation style
steps.body: Choose from the available text effects, such as highlighting, underlining, or animating the selection, and preview each option.

steps.heading: Save your changes
steps.body: Click save to apply the effect and close the editor, then view the live page to confirm it looks right.

faq.question: Can I highlight just one word instead of a whole sentence?
faq.answer: Yes, select only the specific text you want to style before applying the highlight or animation effect.

faq.question: What's the difference between highlighting and underlining text in Squarespace?
faq.answer: Highlighting adds a colored background behind the text, while underlining adds a line beneath it — both are separate style options in the text editor.

faq.question: Will highlight effects work the same on mobile?
faq.answer: Effects generally carry over to mobile, but it's worth previewing the mobile view separately to confirm the styling still looks right on smaller screens.

faq.question: How much text effect is too much?
faq.answer: Reserve highlighting and animation for headlines or key points — applying it to large blocks of text can make a page feel cluttered.
